init.sql team_members/invites/note_shares select policies use 'm.team_id = team_id' which binds to the inner alias (tautology) so any member of any team can read all members/invites/shares; team_members policy also self-queries team_members (recursive RLS); profiles 'find by email' using(true) exposes all emails.

inviteToTeam in app/teams/actions.ts does no role check and just upserts team_members; the insert policy allows 'user_id = auth.uid()' so authorization is not enforced; no remove-member feature exists.
team_members insert policy 'owners can add' has 'or user_id = auth.uid()' so any user can insert themselves into any team by id via direct PostgREST write.
No invite tokens: inviteToTeam directly adds an existing profile as a member (status accepted); no expiry, single-use or acceptance step.

note_shares insert policy checks team membership with the tautological 'm.team_id = team_id' so notes can be shared into any team by a member of any team; no delete policy or unshare/leave feature so access cannot be removed.
No rate limiting or per-team invite cap anywhere.
handle_new_user is security definer with set search_path = '' but the team_members select policy queries its own table (recursive RLS) and no definer helper is used to avoid it.

Create team, share note and invite exist but invite only works for already-registered emails, adds them instantly with no email or acceptance, and the self-referencing team_members policy would likely raise infinite recursion.

init.sql notes select policy requires active team_members row for notes.team_id; team_members select limited to own user_id; teams select by creator or membership; non-members cannot read team notes or member list.
team_members insert/update policies restrict to teams.created_by enforced by RLS (server-side), but there is no remove-member feature and no role model beyond creator.
team_members insert requires caller to be teams.created_by, so a user cannot add themselves to another team; there is no role column to set.
No invite tokens: pending rows keyed by email are bound by handle_new_user at auth.users insert (before email confirmation), with no token, expiry or single-use.

shareNote updates notes.team_id; RLS update policy requires owner (user_id = auth.uid()) and active membership of target team; setting team_id null unshares; leaving is not built but no risk left open.
No rate limiting or per-team invite cap.
Policies reference team_members from notes/teams without self-reference in team_members policy (no recursion); handle_new_user security definer sets search_path = ''.
Teams, invites and note sharing are built but pending invites only activate in the signup trigger so already-registered invitees never become active members; no accept flow or member removal.

Sessions are random 32-byte opaque tokens generated at runtime; no secret in source.
createSession sets expires_at 7 days and requireAuth checks expires_at > now.
Opaque server-side session tokens looked up in the sessions table.
All notes queries in server.js include 'AND user_id = ?' with req.user.id (GET filter, PATCH, DELETE).
All queries use better-sqlite3 prepared statements with placeholders; the dynamic UPDATE only concatenates fixed column fragments.
No rate limiting or throttling on /auth/signup or /auth/login.
Login returns a generic 'Invalid email or password' but signup returns 409 'Email is already registered' and login skips scrypt for unknown emails (timing difference).
No CORS middleware at all, so no origin is allowed with credentials.
No web client; token is returned as a bearer token in JSON, no localStorage use.
Sessions last 7 days and are stored server-side (revocable by deleting rows).

create_note RPC in init.sql does single conditional UPDATE profiles SET credits=credits-1 WHERE id=auth.uid() AND credits>0 and raises if not found.
profiles has only a select policy (no update policy) so authenticated clients cannot change credits; only the security-definer function writes it.

Deduction runs server-side inside create_note before insert, and 'revoke insert on public.notes from authenticated' means a direct client insert cannot bypass it; 0 credits raises 'Not enough credits'.
credits default 5 is set on profile row creation via handle_new_user trigger on auth.users insert, once per user.
Deduction and note insert occur in the same plpgsql function/transaction so a failed insert rolls back the credit decrement.
